question_text: An open copper vessel of mass 20 kg is at a temperature of $150^\circ$ C. Water of mass 0.1 kg at $20^\circ$ C is poured into the vessel. The temperature of the mixture becomes $140^\circ$ C. Assume that there is no loss of heat to the surroundings. (Take specific heat capacity of copper = 40 $	imes 10^2$ J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$; specific heat capacity of water 4$	imes 10^3$ J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$; specific latent heat of vaporization of water 25$	imes 10^5$ J kg$^{-1}$)
